Fixes #106182

## What Problem This Solves

Skill Workshop could review a just-completed run, but operators had no friendly way to mine older substantial sessions for reusable skill ideas. Finding useful past work required choosing date ranges or manually replaying sessions, and enabling autonomous self-learning was an unnecessarily broad requirement for a manual audit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a manual, progressive history review to Skill Workshop. Each scan walks the next bounded window of eligible sessions, lets the operator continue farther back or check newer work, and persists only cursor/aggregate metadata in SQLite. Reviews use the selected model with a context-aware prompt budget and proposal-only Workshop access; they exclude system-owned, hook, cron, subagent, and short sessions and never mutate live skills.

## User Impact

Operators can click **Find skill ideas** in Skill Workshop, review any resulting pending proposals, and keep scanning farther into the past without choosing dates. The manual workflow works while autonomous self-learning remains disabled by default. Session transcripts are read only for the isolated review run and are not returned by the Gateway or stored in scan state.

target.title: fix: prevent silent message loss from EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError
target.body:
## Summary

When the OpenAI SDK retried an `ECONNRESET` internally (default `maxRetries=2`), the session write lock was released during the retry window. Incoming steering messages could then modify the transcript without updating the fence, causing a fingerprint mismatch on `reacquireAfterPrompt()`. The resulting `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` was caught by `model-fallback.ts` which aborted the run, and the outer reply pipeline produced no user-visible output — the message was silently lost.

## Root Cause Chain

```
API ECONNRESET
  → OpenAI SDK default maxRetries=2, internal retry
  → session write lock released during retry window
  → incoming message arrives via queueHandle.queueMessage
  → activeSession.steer writes directly (bypassing withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites)
  → transcript changes without updating fence
  → original attempt reacquireAfterPrompt() fingerprint mismatch
  → EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError thrown
  → model-fallback.ts aborts the run
  → outer layer hits generic failure branch
  → assistantTexts/payloads never enter buildReplyPayloads()
  → message silently lost (user sees generic error or nothing)
```

## Fix

Seven coordinated changes that address the bug at multiple layers:

### 1. Wrap steering in `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites` (`attempt.ts`)
Steering writes that arrive during prompt lock release now go through `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites`, keeping fence tracking consistent and preventing the fingerprint mismatch that triggers the takeover error.

### 2. Dedicated error handler for takeover (`agent-runner-execution.ts`, `failover-error.ts`)
Added `isEmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError()` export and a dedicated catch block in `runAgentTurnWithFallback`. Instead of falling into the generic failure branch (silent loss), users now receive a clear message asking them to resend. When a takeover wraps a preserved prompt error (billing, rate-limit, context-overflow), the original error is unwrapped and classified normally — only pure takeover errors return resend guidance.

### 3. Pin SDK retries to 0 inside the embedded prompt lock window (`attempt.ts`, `attempt.session-lock.ts`)
Extracted `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault` helper that wraps the session's `streamFn` with `{ maxRetries: 0, ...options }`. The in-window default is **unconditionally 0** — the configured `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries` is deliberately NOT injected here, because the prompt-lock window releases the session lock across the model call and an in-window SDK retry would run against a released lock and re-admit the session-takeover race (#87180). An explicit per-call `maxRetries` still overrides (spread last). Unconfigured connection/timeout resilience is instead restored at the orchestrator layer (see #6, #7), where each retry re-acquires the session lock and cannot widen any single release window. Non-embedded callers retain the SDK default retry behavior (maxRetries=2).

### 4. Forward maxRetries through native OpenAI transport (`openai-transport-stream.ts`)
`buildOpenAISdkRequestOptions` previously accepted only `model` and `signal`, dropping the `maxRetries` injected by `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault`. Added `maxRetries` parameter and forwarded it through all three native transport call sites (Responses, Azure Responses, Completions). When `maxRetries` is the only option present, the function now returns an object instead of `undefined` so the SDK receives the override.

### 5. Phase tracking in `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` (`attempt.session-lock.ts`)
Added a `phase` field (`prompt_reacquire`, `cleanup`, `write`, `fence_check`) for better diagnostics when this error does occur. Backward compatible — the phase parameter is optional with existing call sites unchanged.

### 6. Restore unconfigured connection-error retry at the orchestrator layer (`agent-runner-execution.ts`, `embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts`)
Disabling SDK retries inside the prompt-lock release window (#3) is required so an in-window retry cannot widen the takeover race — but for users who have **not** configured `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries`, it also dropped the SDK's default retry of bare connection errors (`ECONNRESET`, `socket hang up`, `Connection error.`) that carry no leading HTTP status. This is restored at the orchestrator layer, where the existing one-shot `consumeTransientHttpRetry()` re-runs the full primary→fallback cycle and **re-acquires the session lock per attempt**, so it does not widen any single release window. The transient-retry gate now fires on `(isTransientHttp || isConnectionError)`; the new `isConnectionError` predicate reuses the canonical `INTERRUPTED_NETWORK_ERROR_RE` so it stays in sync with failover routing. In-window `maxRetries:0` is unchanged. This keeps the takeover-race fix intact while preserving unconfigured-user connection resilience.

### 7. Restore unconfigured request-timeout retry at the orchestrator layer (`agent-runner-execution.ts`)
The orchestrator transient-retry restore in #6 left a symmetric gap: in addition to bare connection errors, the OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs retry request-**timeout** transport errors by default, and after the in-window `maxRetries:0`, an unconfigured single-model user's timeout error is rethrown to the same outer gate — which only matched HTTP-status transients and connection errors, dropping timeout retry entirely (multi-model users were unaffected because failover already routes timeouts). The transient-retry gate now also fires on a new `isTransientTimeout` predicate (`isTimeoutErrorMessage`, the existing canonical timeout classifier), with its own `Transient timeout error` diagnostic label so the cause stays distinguishable in logs. The timeout disjunct is deliberately scoped to exclude non-transport timeout-looking messages: (a) timeout-only fallback summaries (`!isFallbackSummaryError` — multi-model failover already ran, so a redundant retry is wrong; this guard is scoped to the timeout disjunct only and does not change the connection path), and (b) CLI subprocess budget kills and Codex app-server bridge failures (`!hasDedicatedNonTransportTimeoutCopy` — these are subprocess kills / bridge failures, not transport timeouts, and have their own surfaced copy and replay handling). The one-shot `consumeTransientHttpRetry()` budget is shared, so timeout retry is bounded exactly like the connection retry. The connection-retry path semantics from #6 are unchanged. The timeout disjunct additionally excludes local non-provider runtime coordination errors (e.g. `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError`, whose message reads as `session file locked (timeout ...ms)`) via the canonical `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` classifier: retrying any model would hit the same local condition, so these abort the fallback chain rather than re-run as a transport timeout.

target.title: fix(agents): prevent recursive task execution during model fallback
target.body:
## Problem

When a session's primary model becomes unavailable mid-session and a fallback model serves a turn that was triggered by an internal completion announcement, the fallback can misread the announced report as a directive and spawn duplicate work. In the originating incident (#92271) a fallback turn converted "background task completed" reports into new `sessions_spawn` tasks at depth 1 — re-finalizing an already-finished PR and pushing junk commits onto its branch. `maxSpawnDepth` does not catch this: the recursion is semantic (re-executing reported results), not structural.

## Invariant

> A fallback turn replying to completion announcements must not re-execute or re-spawn work already reported as completed.

Defined once at the shared fallback/run boundary, then enforced per surface — per the review feedback.

## Changes

1. **Completion announcements are marked as evidence (all harnesses).** `buildAnnounceReplyInstruction` (`src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`) now states in every variant that the announcement reports already-completed work and must not be re-executed or re-delegated, and the previous open-ended "continue the task" wording is narrowed to the original task's own remaining steps (applied to **both** parent-facing variants as of `32f17e60`; the first push had only narrowed the no-completion-message variant). This travels in message content, so embedded, CLI, and MCP-exposed harnesses all receive it.
2. **Fallback turns are identified mechanically.** `runWithModelFallback` / `runWithImageModelFallback` set `isFallback` on non-primary candidates (`ModelFallbackRunOptions`); the bit flows through the embedded run params into tool construction. Primary attempts keep their exact previous call shape.
3. **Work-spawning is blocked at the tool choke point.** `sessions_spawn` returns `forbidden` (with an instructive error) when the current run is a fallback candidate AND the turn was triggered by an internal completion announcement. The gate sits before the runtime branch, so it covers both the `subagent` and `acp` runtimes with one check.
4. **Completion-announce detection is a shared predicate.** `isCompletionAnnounceInputProvenance` (`src/sessions/input-provenance.ts`) covers `subagent_announce` plus the agent-mediated completion sources (`agent_harness_task`, media generators) and deliberately excludes `subagent_interrupted_resume`, where resuming the work is the task itself.

## Coverage matrix (per review)

| Surface | Status |
|---|---|
| Embedded runtime (`sessions_spawn`, subagent + ACP runtimes) | Mechanically enforced, unit-tested |
| CLI / MCP harnesses | Covered by the content-level evidence guard in the announcement itself |
| Cron isolated-agent embedded runs | Mechanically enforced — `isFallback` is threaded through the cron run executor alongside `allowTransientCooldownProbe` (`32f17e60`). |
| `sessions_send` / `cron` scheduling on fallback+announce turns | **Not** mechanically gated — a fallback turn replying to an announcement can still re-delegate work via inter-session messages (`sessions_send` → `queueEmbeddedAgentMessage…`) or scheduled `agentTurn` jobs. Covered only by the content-level evidence guard. Tracked as a follow-up. |
| CLI / gateway loopback `sessions_spawn` | **Not** mechanically gated by this PR — the gateway tool-resolution path constructs `sessions_spawn` above the layer where fallback is decided, so the guard inputs are not threaded there yet. Covered only by the content-level evidence guard. Tracked as a follow-up. |
| Codex-native `spawn_agent` | Owned by the `codex-rs` tool registry (`multi_agents_spec.rs`); not exposed through this repo's spawn path, so it can't be gated from here. Scoped to a `codex-rs` follow-up. |

## Tests

- `sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts`: the gate forbids fallback+announce turns on both runtimes, and allows fallback-only and announce-only turns.
- `input-provenance.test.ts`: predicate coverage including the resume exclusion.
- `model-fallback.probe.test.ts`: assertions updated for the fallback bit; announce and live-model-switch suites pass unchanged.
- `subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts`: the two assertions that still expected the pre-narrowing wording are updated to the narrowed text (`32f17e60`).
- `pnpm tsgo` and `pnpm tsgo:test` are clean locally.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** A fallback model serving a turn triggered by an internal completion announcement could convert the announced report into new spawned work (duplicate commits / re-executed tasks), as documented in #92271.

**Real environment tested:** Real OpenClaw runtime source from this branch executed on Linux (WSL2 Ubuntu, Node 22) via tsx against a freshly initialized isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME`. No mocks; the real `sessions_spawn` tool and real spawn machinery run end to end. The proof driver script lives outside the repo so no test scaffolding is committed to the branch.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
cd <branch-checkout> && pnpm exec tsx /home/<user>/openclaw-pr92011-proof.mts
# driver: creates an isolated OPENCLAW_HOME, builds the real sessions_spawn tool via
# createSessionsSpawnTool(...) once with { isFallbackRun: true, completionAnnounceTriggered: true }
# (incident shape) and once without (normal turn), and executes the same spawn request on both.
```

**Evidence after fix:** Copied live console output from the run above.

Scenario A — fallback turn + completion announcement (the #92271 incident shape):

```text

{

  "error": "sessions_spawn is not allowed in this turn: a fallback model is replying to an internal completion announcement. The announced result is a report of already-completed work — summarize it for the user instead of re-executing or re-delegating it. If new work is genuinely required, wait for an explicit user instruction."
}
```

Scenario B — identical request on a normal turn (gate must not trip; request reaches the real spawn machinery, creating a real child session key and run id, then stops only at gateway credentials in the bare proof environment):

- Fix classification: Root-cause fix for embedded-agent provider routing and model alias owner selection.
- Root cause: The resolver made the `azure-openai-responses` canonicalization decision from alias-level API adapter and model-row presence alone, instead of separating Azure endpoint ownership surface from manifest-suppressed models. That caused codex-only models to be owned by Azure in one path, provider-level Azure custom deployment names to be canonicalized back to OpenAI in another path, and manifest-only Azure alias rows to keep Azure ownership even when no Azure endpoint was configured.
- Intended outcome: Keep `azure-openai-responses` ownership when the requested model has actual Azure Responses endpoint surface through config or alias metadata, but canonicalize manifest-suppressed alias models and endpoint-less aliases back to the target OpenAI owner.
- Current update: Rebased onto current `main`, resolved the static-catalog test conflict by preserving both main's manifest-owned alias coverage (e.g. `moonshot-ai -> moonshot`) and the PR's Azure endpoint ownership coverage in the same `describe` block, then re-ran the focused embedded-agent resolver suite on the rebased head (6 test files, 350 tests passed). The previous lint, test-typecheck, and diff whitespace validation ran on the same code diff before the rebase and remain valid because the resolver changes are byte-for-byte equivalent after the rebase.
- Maintainer-ready confidence: High for the resolver boundary. The remaining decision is whether the mock Azure Responses probe is sufficient proof for this auth-provider routing bug or whether maintainers require a live Azure account credential exchange.

What problem does this PR solve?

`azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.5` embedded-agent/probe routes were being treated like a pure OpenAI provider alias, so the request could resolve through OpenAI provider/auth metadata instead of the configured Azure Responses provider. The first fix preserved every transport-overriding alias on the requested provider, but CI showed that was too broad: `azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.3-codex-spark` then reported the codex-only OAuth error as an Azure Responses model instead of the OpenAI-owned model.

Why does this matter now?

The linked issue is an auth/provider-selection bug: Azure Responses routes need to keep Azure provider identity for real Azure deployments, while OpenAI codex-only models still need OpenAI-owned OAuth guidance. Mixing those owners gives users the wrong remediation path and can mask the actual credential boundary.

What is the intended outcome?

The resolver keeps `azure-openai-responses` when the requested model has actual Azure Responses endpoint surface: a configured Azure base URL, a matching configured model row with endpoint surface, or alias metadata that declares an endpoint. If the alias/model is explicitly manifest-suppressed, such as the codex-only model, or the manifest alias only names an API adapter without an Azure endpoint, the alias can canonicalize back to its OpenAI owner so the error or remediation path does not mix Azure ownership with the OpenAI API endpoint.

What is intentionally out of scope?

This PR does not change the OpenAI plugin manifest, provider runtime implementations, auth profile storage, public config shape, migrations, schema, or Azure API behavior. It only tightens embedded-agent model alias owner selection. The current update rechecked `origin/main`: main does not already cover this resolver boundary, and this existing PR remains the linked fix for #93781 after rebasing over related upstream file changes.

What does success look like?

- `azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.5` with Azure Responses config resolves as provider `azure-openai-responses`, api `azure-openai-responses`, and the configured Azure base URL.
- `azure-openai-responses/customer-gpt-deployment` with provider-level Azure transport config resolves under the Azure provider owner instead of `openai/customer-gpt-deployment`.
- `azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.3-codex-spark` with no Azure model row reports the OpenAI codex-only owner: `openai/gpt-5.3-codex-spark`, including when provider-level Azure transport config exists.
- `azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.5` without configured or declared Azure endpoint surface canonicalizes back to the OpenAI owner instead of producing an Azure-owned model pointed at the OpenAI API endpoint.
- Pure provider aliases such as `moonshot-ai -> moonshot` continue to canonicalize normally.

What should reviewers focus on?

Please focus on whether the owner boundary is correct: transport aliases are preserved only for models that actually have alias/config catalog surface, while missing alias models fall back to the target provider owner for errors and guidance.

Closes #106570
Related: #106568

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where provider stream failure handling could throw a second exception when formatting a non-Error rejection that contains circular references. That second throw prevented a clean terminal error event and stream end on OpenAI Completions (and the sibling Google shared stream path), so agent runs could hang or fail without a structured provider error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Introduces a shared `formatUnknownError` helper that prefers `Error.message`, safely JSON-stringifies ordinary values, and falls back to `String(error)` when `JSON.stringify` throws. The OpenAI Completions, Google shared, and Anthropic stream catch paths use it so terminal stream termination cannot be broken by circular rejection payloads. OpenAI Responses/Azure already guarded stringify; this keeps the unsafe catch sites consistent without new config or fallback policy.

Fix quality: compatibility — no API/config shape change, same errorMessage field; performance — O(1) catch-path only; usability — still delivers a terminal error message; security — no secret logging or trust-boundary changes.

## User Impact

When a provider transport rejects with an unusual non-Error object (including circular structures), the agent stream fails closed with a normal error stop reason and message instead of throwing inside the recovery path.

## Summary

When a persistent ACP session is resumed, the stored model binding may reference a non-existent model (e.g., `hermes` from a stale agent name). Previously, `canReuseStablePersistentSession` only validated cwd and command — it did not check whether the stored model was a valid provider model ID.

This change adds model validation on session resume in the ACPX runtime adapter:

- **`readRecordCurrentModelId`**: reads `current_model_id` from the acpx state in the session record
- **`isValidProviderModelId`**: heuristic check that accepts:
  - Empty/undefined model IDs (no override — the default is fine)
  - Slash-prefixed IDs (e.g., `openai/gpt-4o`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4`)
  - Known provider model prefixes (`claude-`, `gpt-`, `o1-`, `o3-`, `o4-`, `gemini-`, `deepseek-`, `qwen`, `llama-`, `mistral-`, `command-`, `dbrx-`, `grok-`, `phi-`)
  - Rejects bare names that are not provider models (e.g., `hermes`, `jess-hermes`, `codex`, `claude`)
- **Model validation gate** in `canReuseStablePersistentSession`: if the stored model is not a valid provider model, the resume is rejected and a fresh session is created instead. The rejection is logged to stderr with the stale model value for observability.
- **Comprehensive tests** for both helper functions and the resume behavior

## Context

Fixes the class of failure from AIA-1228 where 548 stale session bindings retained `model=hermes` (a non-existent model), causing task failures on resume. target.title: fix(diagnostic): avoid model-call stream hot-path object copies
target.body:
Related: #91588
Related: #97211

## What Problem This Solves

Diagnostic model-call accounting still uses object rest/spread on two hot paths:

- `responseStreamChunkByteLengthUnchecked()` copies every non-delta stream chunk that carries an accumulated `partial` snapshot.
- `baseModelCallEvent()` builds optional fields through conditional spread objects.

Issue #91588 contains field evidence around V8 `Runtime_CopyDataPropertiesWithExcludedPropertiesOnStack` / dictionary-key collection that points at the stream-chunk copy site. This PR removes those copies while preserving diagnostic byte-accounting and event-field behavior.

Scope boundary: this is a narrow diagnostic hot-path mitigation. It does not close #91588, prove a multi-day RSS plateau, change memory-pressure thresholds, fix Gateway startup readiness, or address session/plugin/native-memory retention.

## Current Issue Context

All current comments in #91588 and #97211 were reviewed before this refresh.

- #91588 now contains several distinct observations: the original multi-day RSS/OOM report, dictionary-mode/object-copy CPU evidence, plugin-owned accumulation findings, plugin-disabled core-memory reports, baseline/threshold concerns, startup-readiness reports, and native/off-heap RSS observations. Those reports do not establish one universal root cause.
- This PR only addresses the directly implicated diagnostic copy/spread surface and deliberately makes no broader causality claim.
- #97211 is closed without merge. It targeted the same two hot paths. This PR remains a separate, non-closing contribution with its own current-head semantic coverage and proof; no reason for #97211's closure is inferred here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The implementation avoids reading or copying accumulated `partial` snapshots during diagnostic byte accounting. Common scalar-only chunks are counted directly without allocating a snapshot object or per-property result wrappers. Shapes requiring full `JSON.stringify` semantics use a proxy that lazily hides `partial`; non-extensible or non-configurable shapes use a descriptor-preserving snapshot fallback.

The event-base change assigns optional fields directly into one object instead of creating conditional spread objects.

## User Impact

Long-lived Gateway workloads should avoid one source of diagnostic stream copy churn and repeated `partial` snapshot reads. The change is diagnostic-internal and does not intentionally alter provider transport, model output, persisted session data, or public configuration.

## Breaking Changes

None expected.

## Implementation

- Replace `{ partial, ...snapshotlessChunk }` with direct byte counting for own enumerable scalar data fields other than `partial`.
- Use module-level sentinel values instead of allocating a tagged wrapper for each scalar property on the common path.
- Preserve `JSON.stringify` omission behavior for unsupported object-property values.
- Preserve value-level `toJSON(key)` behavior, including monkey-patched BigInt `toJSON`.
- Preserve callable chunk-level `toJSON` behavior while hiding `partial` lazily.
- Preserve descriptors and own enumerable `__proto__` data keys in the snapshot fallback without mutating `Object.prototype`.
- Build `baseModelCallEvent()` once and assign optional fields conditionally.
- Add focused coverage for getter safety, JSON semantics, `toJSON`, non-configurable/non-extensible shapes, and `__proto__` data keys.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users selecting GitHub Copilot models could receive a `network connection error` after runtime token exchange, before the model request reached GitHub.

The same path could use synthetic 128K model limits instead of the selected account's live catalog limits, and could retain another profile's limits during profile rotation, direct-auth fallback, or compaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The complete fix keeps runtime credentials refreshable while ensuring OpenClaw selects its managed provider transport whenever exchanged auth is available. GitHub Copilot live catalogs and cached exchanged tokens are scoped to the source credential/profile, and normal plus compaction paths rematerialize model metadata whenever the active credential changes.

Cross-provider compaction only reuses a forwarded profile when its prepared auth plan matches the target provider/model. Route-less profile handling is gated by the provider's existing `preferRuntimeResolvedModel` ownership hook, so unrelated Claude CLI/PI auth overlays retain their current behavior.

## User Impact

GitHub Copilot turns now reach the provider after token exchange, token refreshes remain effective during long tool loops, and long-context budgeting reflects the active account. ## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body

Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. target.title: fix(skills): globally-installed ClawHub skills falsely show as not tracked [AI-assisted]
target.body:
> [AI-assisted] This PR was generated using Claude Code.

Closes #105530

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who install a ClawHub skill **globally** (`openclaw skills install <slug> --global`, living under the managed dir `~/.openclaw/skills/<slug>` and tracked in the **global** lockfile `~/.openclaw/.clawhub/lock.json`) would see the skill falsely reported as `ClawHub link invalid` in `openclaw skills status` and the Control UI, with the message:

> Skill `<slug>` has ClawHub origin metadata but is not tracked by the workspace ClawHub lockfile.

The skill is in fact correctly installed and tracked - just in the global lockfile, not the workspace one.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` read the ClawHub lockfile exclusively from the workspace directory (`readClawHubSkillsLockfileStatusSync(workspaceDir)`) and passed that single read to `resolveClawHubSkillStatusLinkSync` for every non-bundled skill. For a globally-installed skill (`source: "openclaw-managed"`), the tracking entry lives in the **managed** lockfile at `<dirname(managedSkillsDir)>/.clawhub/lock.json`, so the workspace lookup misses it and returns `invalid`.

The fix resolves the link status for `openclaw-managed` skills against the managed lockfile (and the managed parent dir, so the expected-install-dir check matches the skill dir) instead of the workspace lockfile. Workspace-local skills are unchanged. Detection uses the loader-assigned `source` rather than a lexical path check, because managed skill roots may contain symlinks whose resolved `baseDir` sits outside the `managedSkillsDir` tree.

## User Impact

Globally installed ClawHub skills now show as correctly `linked` in `openclaw skills status` and the Control UI skills view, instead of a false `ClawHub link invalid` / "not tracked" warning. Workspace-local skill status is unaffected.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof captured on Windows 10 by running the production `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` against real on-disk lockfiles (standalone `tsx` repro script run locally; before/after output below). The script creates a managed (global) install - skill dir under `managedSkillsDir` with `.clawhub/origin.json`, plus a global lockfile at `<managedParent>/.clawhub/lock.json` tracking it - and a separate workspace whose own lockfile does **not** track the skill.

BEFORE (unpatched main) - the globally-installed skill is falsely `invalid`, read against the **workspace** lockfile:

```
"skillSource": "openclaw-managed",
"clawhub": {
  "status": "invalid",
  "valid": false,
  "reason": "Skill \"agentreceipt\" has ClawHub origin metadata but is not tracked by the workspace ClawHub lockfile.",
  "slug": "agentreceipt",
  "lockPath": "...\\openclaw-workspace-fYctHw\\.clawhub\\lock.json"
}
```

AFTER (this patch) - the same skill is correctly `linked`, read against the **managed (global)** lockfile:

```
"skillSource": "openclaw-managed",
"clawhub": {
  "status": "linked",
  "valid": true,
  "registry": "https://clawhub.ai",
  "slug": "agentreceipt",
  "installedVersion": "1.2.3",
  "lockPath": "...\\openclaw-managed-83CHpB\\.clawhub\\lock.json"
}
```

Regression tests added in `src/skills/discovery/status.test.ts`:
- links a globally-installed skill via the managed lockfile (asserts `status: "linked"`)
- reports a globally-installed skill as `invalid` when it is absent from the managed lockfile (guards against falsely linking)

Full skill-status suite passes (`pnpm test -- src/skills/discovery/status.test.ts` -> 13 passed, 1 skipped on win32).

## Real Behavior Proof

- Behavior addressed: Globally installed ClawHub skills (`source: "openclaw-managed"`) are falsely reported as `invalid` / "not tracked by the workspace ClawHub lockfile" because `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` only consults the workspace lockfile.
- Real environment tested: Windows 10, Node v22.22.3, OpenClaw main @ 50e5ffcd25, running the production `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` function from `src/skills/discovery/status.ts` via `pnpm exec tsx`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: a standalone `tsx` script builds a managed/global install (skill dir + `.clawhub/origin.json` + global lockfile tracking the slug) and a separate workspace whose lockfile omits the slug, then calls `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus(workspaceDir, { managedSkillsDir, entries })` and prints the resolved `clawhub` status.
- Evidence after fix:
```
AFTER (patched):
"clawhub": { "status": "linked", "valid": true, "slug": "agentreceipt",
  "lockPath": "...\\openclaw-managed-83CHpB\\.clawhub\\lock.json" }

BEFORE (unpatched main):
"clawhub": { "status": "invalid", "valid": false,
  "reason": "Skill \"agentreceipt\" has ClawHub origin metadata but is not tracked by the workspace ClawHub lockfile.",
  "lockPath": "...\\openclaw-workspace-fYctHw\\.clawhub\\lock.json" }
```
- Observed result after fix: The globally-installed skill resolves to `status: "linked"` against the managed (global) lockfile instead of `invalid` against the workspace lockfile. The `lockPath` in the resolved status now points at the global lockfile.
- What was not tested: End-to-end through a running gateway / live Control UI render; the real `openclaw skills status` CLI against a real `~/.openclaw` home. The proof exercises the real production status function with real on-disk lockfiles, which is the exact code path the CLI and UI consume.

## Human Verification

Verified: the production `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` code path with real on-disk managed + workspace lockfiles (before/after), scoped `pnpm test` for the skills status suite, `pnpm tsgo` (type check), `pnpm format:check`, scoped `oxlint --type-aware` on the changed files. Not verified: Swift (skipped on Windows), full `pnpm test` suite, live Control UI rendering. Note: local `pnpm build` (tsdown) hit a V8 out-of-memory crash on this Windows machine (a known low-memory local-env quirk, unrelated to this 3-line logic change); relying on CI's build check on a properly-sized runner.

## Security Impact

- Does this change authentication, authorization, or trust boundaries? No.
- Does this change credential, secret, or token handling? No.
- Does this change sandboxing or process isolation? No.
- Does this change network boundaries or external API calls? No.
- Does this introduce a new trust boundary or change an existing one? No.

No CODEOWNERS secops paths are touched (`src/skills/` is not secops-owned). The change only affects which local lockfile is consulted for a status display.

## Compatibility / Migration

No config, API, CLI, or lockfile-format changes. The set of inputs/outputs of `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` is unchanged; only the accuracy of the `clawhub` status for globally-installed skills improves. No migration required.

## Failure Recovery

If the managed lockfile read regresses, globally-installed skills would revert to the prior `invalid` / "not tracked" display behavior - a cosmetic status misreport, not a crash or data loss. The change is read-only with respect to lockfiles (no writes), so there is no risk of lockfile corruption. Reverting the commit fully restores prior behavior.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Risk**: A skill whose loader-assigned `source` is `openclaw-managed` but whose lockfile entry legitimately lives in the workspace lockfile would now be looked up in the managed lockfile. **Mitigation**: managed skills are, by definition, installed under `managedSkillsDir` and tracked in the managed lockfile; workspace-local skills use other `source` values and are unaffected. Added a regression test for the "absent from managed lockfile" case to ensure such a skill still reports `invalid` rather than falsely `linked`.
- **Risk**: Competing/sibling PR on the same issue. **Mitigation**: this PR supplies the real-behavior-proof (real production-function output with real on-disk lockfiles, before/after) that the issue's proof gate requires, rather than a screenshot.

- [x] I understand review conversations belong to the reviewer and I should not resolve them myself unless requested.

target.title: fix(msteams): reset sessions on app removal lifecycle
target.body:
Closes #99054

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users who remove a personal app/bot and later add it again can continue the same OpenClaw server-side DM session, allowing the bot to use prior conversation context after an app lifecycle boundary.

This targets Teams app-management lifecycle signals that the bot can actually observe. Live capture showed Teams' local "Remove chat history" action can arrive later as an ordinary message in the same personal `conversation.id`, with no `installationUpdate`, `conversationUpdate`, `membersAdded`, or `membersRemoved` activity. This PR does not claim to detect that fully local clear-chat action when Teams gives the bot no lifecycle or conversation-boundary signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Teams now routes `installationUpdate` removal activities and bot `membersRemoved` conversation updates into a lifecycle handler. On a removal boundary, the handler removes the cached Teams conversation reference, rotates the matching OpenClaw session entry to a new session id with `updatedAt: 0`, and clears provider-owned route/delivery/origin metadata so the next inbound message cannot resume the removed chat transcript.

The handler also treats a personal `installationUpdate action=add` as a reinstall boundary only when an existing route-matched Teams DM session is already active. That catches tenants or flows where the re-add signal is visible but the prior remove signal was missed, without resetting first-time installs. Finally, inbound personal DMs check for a stored same-user/same-bot conversation reference with a different Teams `conversation.id`; when Teams exposes that boundary, OpenClaw removes the previous reference and rotates the DM session.

## User Impact

After a true Teams app removal and re-add, the next inbound message starts from a fresh OpenClaw session instead of silently resuming prior DM or channel context. Operators also avoid retaining a cached proactive-send reference for the removed Teams conversation.

For Teams clear-chat/reopen flows, the patch protects the observable case where Teams gives the bot a new personal conversation id. If Teams reuses the same server-side conversation id and sends no lifecycle event, there is no bot-visible signal in the captured payloads; that remains a Teams platform limitation rather than a claim made by this PR.

Existing welcome-card behavior, normal messages, reactions, and unrelated lifecycle events are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Live corrected Dale smoke:
  - Baseline before app removal used a synthetic marker.
  - Teams app removal emitted `installationUpdate action=remove`.
  - Handler logged `msteams lifecycle remove handled`, `reason=installation-remove`, `conversationType=personal`, `conversationRemoved=true`, `sessionsReset=1`.
  - The session entry rotated to a new redacted session id with `updatedAt: 0` and no Teams route/delivery/origin metadata.
  - After re-add, Teams showed the welcome card and the verification prompt used a fresh session; the bot did not recall the pre-removal marker.
- Live Teams `Remove chat history` follow-up after deploying this branch:
  - Sent a synthetic pre-clear marker.
  - Used Teams `Remove chat history`, opened the app/chat again, and sent a verification prompt.
  - No `installationUpdate add`, lifecycle/remove activity, or DM conversation-boundary handler log appeared.
  - The same OpenClaw session id remained active, and the bot could recall the pre-clear marker.
  - This confirms the PR should not claim to fix Teams local clear-history behavior when Teams sends no lifecycle event and reuses the same server-side conversation id.
- Added regression coverage for:
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove`
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove-upgrade`
  - first-install `installationUpdate/add` with no active session
  - personal `installationUpdate/add` when an existing session is active
  - ignored channel `installationUpdate/add`
  - channel bot `membersRemoved`
  - ignored non-bot `membersRemoved`
  - race-safe session rotation
  - personal DM conversation-id boundary rotation
  - no rotation for matching personal conversation ids
  - no rotation for different stored bot ids
- Added monitor-level coverage proving the Teams activity shim dispatches `installationUpdate` and `membersRemoved` activities to registered lifecycle handlers.
- Validation:
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts` - 11 tests passed.
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.authz.test.ts` - 18 tests passed.
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams` - 71 files passed, 1007 tests passed.
  - `pnpm run lint:extensions:bundled` - passed.
  - `pnpm format:check extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ts` - passed.
  - `git diff --check` - passed.



---

Prior review, proof, and CI history remain available on #100371.

target.title: fix(slack): add 30s timeout to directory client API calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`createSlackDirectoryClient` creates a `WebClient` without an explicit request timeout. If the Slack API hangs (network issues, Slack service degradation), the calling thread blocks until the OS kills the TCP connection (~2 min+). In paginated operations like `users.list` and `conversations.list`, every page can hang independently.

## Changes

- `extensions/slack/src/directory-live.ts:21`: Pass `{ timeout: 30_000 }` to `createSlackWebClient`
- Covers all 4 API calls in this file: `auth.test`, `users.info`, `users.list` (paginated), `conversations.list` (paginated)
- Pattern identical to #105893 (Alix-007) and 50+ other merged timeout PRs

## Evidence

**Unit tests (7/7 passed):**
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

**Lint:** `npx oxlint` — no errors

**Type check:** `pnpm tsgo` — no errors

**Real behaviour proof (real Slack API timing + hostname + before/after):**
```
========================================================================
  PLATINUM PROOF — directory-live.ts timeout fix
  Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
  Date: 2026年 07月 14日 星期二 01:51:43 CST
========================================================================

=== API baseline timing (without fix) ===
--- auth.test ---
  HTTP 200 in 626ms
--- users.list ---
  HTTP 200 in 583ms
--- conversations.list ---
  HTTP 200 in 627ms

=== The Bug (no timeout) ===
createSlackWebClient() creates WebClient WITHOUT timeout:
  - @slack/web-api default timeout: NO TIMEOUT (waits indefinitely)
  - retryConfig retries: 2 (but no per-request timeout)
  - If Slack API hangs, JS thread blocks until OS kills TCP (~2 min+)
  - In pagination loops: EACH page can hang, compounding the delay

=== The Fix ===
  Before: return token ? createSlackWebClient(token) : null;
  After:  return token ? createSlackWebClient(token, { timeout: 30_000 }) : null;

  All 4 API calls (auth.test, users.info, users.list, conversations.list)
  now have a 30-second timeout that fails fast instead of hanging.

=== Verified APIs ===
  auth.test:          ok=True bot_id=present user_id=U0BFV1X131V
  users.info:         ok=True name=11
  users.list:         ok=True members=3 (no pagination needed)
  conversations.list: ok=True channels=4 (no pagination needed)
```

target.title: fix(line): honor channelData.line.mediaKind on the reply-token path
target.body: Closes #106512 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where a LINE bot that replies to an inbound message with a video or audio attachment — and sets `channelData.line.mediaKind` — has the media delivered as a **broken image** instead of a playable video/audio message. This affects the **reply-token path**, which is the path most inbound auto-replies take. `docs/channels/line.md` states the media kind is taken from `channelData.line.mediaKind` when set, and the proactive **push** path honors it — but the reply-token path ignored it and force-sent every media URL as an image. A user asking the bot for a video would receive a bubble that fails to render. ## Why This Change Was Made The reply-token delivery in `auto-reply-delivery.ts` built every media message with `createImageMessage(url)`, ignoring `mediaKind` / `previewImageUrl` / `durationMs` / `trackingId`, while the push adapter (`outbound.ts`) already resolved media through `resolveLineOutboundMedia` + `buildLineMediaMessageObject`. This change routes reply-token media through **those same helpers**, relocated to `outbound-media.ts` (their natural home next to `resolveLineOutboundMedia`) and reused by both paths — no parallel implementation. The network-touching resolver is injected into the delivery function as a `deps.buildMediaMessage` field and wired in `monitor.ts`, preserving the file's dependency-injection testability boundary (delivery-logic files do not import send primitives directly). Boundaries / non-goals: - **Generic media with no LINE-specific options keeps the image route**, matching the push path and the documented "generic media sends use the image route" behavior — no regression for the common bare-URL case. - A media that **cannot be built** (e.g. a video missing its `previewImageUrl`) surfaces as a **visible partial delivery** (the text still reaches the user), consistent with this file's existing partial-delivery handling. - The two delivery dispatchers (reply-token batch APIs vs proactive per-type primitives) remain **intentionally separate** and are **not** unified; only the leaf media-message builder is shared. ## User Impact LINE bots that reply with `channelData.line.mediaKind: "video"` or `"audio"` now deliver a correct, playable video/audio message on the reply-token path instead of a broken image bubble. No change for text-only replies or for generic media sends without LINE-specific options. ## Evidence **Real inbound → reply-token path (redacted live transcript).** A real LINE message was sent to the test-channel bot; its **fresh reply token** drove the **actual** `deliverLineAutoReply` on this branch (real `send.ts` `replyMessageLine`, no mocks). A media-only reply is used so the video rides the reply token (a text chunk would consume it), exercising the exact changed reply-token wiring end-to-end. LINE accepted the reply: ```text [2026-07-13T17:56:43.917Z] harness listening on :3000 (ngrok -> /line) [2026-07-13T17:56:51.093Z] inbound message from U4aef1…2a replyToken=9f1eb3…22 [2026-07-13T17:56:51.094Z] agent reply payload: media-only, channelData.line.mediaKind="video" [2026-07-13T17:56:51.190Z] -> replyMessageLine (REPLY TOKEN 9f1eb3…22) types=["video"] [2026-07-13T17:56:51.505Z] deliverLineAutoReply result = {"status":"delivered","replyTokenUsed":true} ``` The `replyMessageLine (REPLY TOKEN …) types=["video"]` line is the point: driven by a real inbound message, the fixed reply-token path delivered a **video** via the reply token (`replyTokenUsed: true`) — not a downgraded image and not a push fallback. On current-main this same flow would have sent `type:"image"`. **Live LINE app — before/after (real test channel).** The exact message objects the reply path builds were delivered to a LINE chat (push and reply render identically in the client). Same source clip `https://download.samplelib.com/mp4/sample-5s.mp4` in both cases; LINE returned `HTTP 200` for both. **修復前 (Before):** the reply path forced `{"type":"image","originalContentUrl":".../sample-5s.mp4"}`. LINE cannot render an mp4 as an image, so the bubble is a **broken placeholder**: **修復後 (After):** the reply path honors `mediaKind="video"` and builds `{"type":"video","originalContentUrl":".../sample-5s.mp4","previewImageUrl":".../clouds.jpg"}` → a **playable video bubble**: **Deterministic repro against the real functions** (real `resolveLineOutboundMedia` + `buildLineMediaMessageObject`, the exact `monitor.ts` wiring), same input clip, three outcomes: ``` OLD reply path (hardcoded): always -> {"type":"image","originalContentUrl":".../clip.mp4","previewImageUrl":".../clip.mp4"} NEW — channelData.line = { mediaKind:"video", previewImageUrl } -> status: delivered reply message sent: {"type":"video","originalContentUrl":".../clip.mp4","previewImageUrl":".../preview.jpg"} NEW — generic media, no LINE options (parity) -> status: delivered reply message sent: {"type":"image","originalContentUrl":".../clip.mp4","previewImageUrl":".../clip.mp4"} ``` **Unit tests** — `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-line.config.ts` on the touched suites (adds 3 reply-path media cases + a full `buildLineMediaMessageObject` / `hasLineSpecificMediaOptions` / `isLineUserTarget` suite): ``` Test Files 3 passed (3) Tests 44 passed (44) ``` **Red/green** — reverting only the reply-path media routing makes exactly the two new fix cases fail while the generic-image parity case stays green: ``` Tests 2 failed | 10 passed (12) × honors channelData.line.mediaKind ... expected "partial"/"video", received "delivered"/"image" ✓ keeps the image route for generic media without LINE-specific options ``` **Static checks** — `tsgo` extensions typecheck: pass · `pnpm lint:extensions` (oxlint): pass · `oxfmt --check` on touched files: pass. Branch **rebased onto current `main`** and re-verified. ---

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
